questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be flexible with your lane position, especially at night.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a cause of motorcycle wobble?
questions.correctAnswerText: Uneven road
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or incorrect tire pressure. Do not try to accelerate out of a wobble.

questions.question: What does a yellow sign with black lettering or symbols mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black lettering or symbols are warning signs. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: What should you do when a vehicle passes you on the left?

options.text: Move as far right as possible to help them pass.
Move to the shoulder to help them pass.
Stay in the center of your lane.
Move to the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Moving to the right increases the risk of a crash. Moving to the left might make the other driver merge back too soon. Stay centered when being passed.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Talk to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: With a passenger, your motorcycle responds more slowly. Ride slower, slow down sooner, and increase your following distance. Always warn your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: What formation is best for a group entering a curve?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Use a single-file line when turning, entering curves, or entering or exiting highways.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in a group?

options.text: Put inexperienced riders at the back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't follow riders too closely.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation and check your mirrors regularly. Choose experienced riders for the front and back of the group. Keep proper space between riders.

questions.question: What formation should a group of three-wheel motorcycles use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file line.
questions.explanation: Three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for a staggered formation. A group of three-wheel motorcycles should travel in a single-file line.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to get a motorcycle endorsement?
questions.correctAnswerText: 18 years old
questions.explanation: You must be at least 18 years old to get a motorcycle endorsement on your driver's license in the District of Columbia.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket while riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool, even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Riding jackets help prevent dehydration and protect you at all times. Many jackets are made to prevent overheating, even in warm weather.

questions.question: What does wearing a riding jacket do in hot weather?

options.text: It can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: You should still wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, in addition to their other safety benefits.

questions.question: What should you do if your rear wheel locks while braking?

options.text: Release the brake until the tire grips again, then re-apply it.
Release the brake and only use the front brake.
Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the brake locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while braking, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What happens to stopping distance when you carry a load in a sidecar?

options.text: It stays the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may increase.
questions.explanation: Adding weight to a motorcycle increases its mass, which makes it take longer to stop. Start slowing down and stopping earlier when you are carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: Which instruction should you NOT give a passenger before riding?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Maintain a large space between yourself and me.
Keep your legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a large space between yourself and me.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to mount the motorcycle after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold onto the handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side of your desired turn. Press on the opposite handgrip to go back to your original direction after you pass the hazard.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an obstacle, slow down as much as possible. Try to hit it at a 90-degree angle, keep the motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and ease off the throttle just before impact.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when being passed?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closer to the passing driver increases collision risk. Riding on the far side may cause them to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance in normal conditions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead in normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: What is the correct way to look when riding?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look through the turn by turning only your head. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help with balance. Your arms should be slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: Which is a bad reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is following the car ahead too closely.
A parked car has someone sitting in the driver's seat.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.
You are passing a person in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn a vehicle or pedestrian before you pass them. If a driver is too close to the car ahead, they may try to pass and cut in front of you. If someone is in a parked car or on the street, sound your horn as you pass them. Do not use your horn just to get attention.

questions.question: Your friend has been drinking and wants to drive. What should you NOT do?

options.text: Ask other friends to talk them out of driving.
Arrange another way for them to get home.
Tell them to use less busy roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell them to use less busy roads.
questions.explanation: Never let someone drive after drinking. Instead, arrange another way for them to get home. Get other friends involved. Keep them busy to slow their drinking. Do not suggest they drive on less busy roads — this is not safe.

questions.question: When another rider is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the middle of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, stay in the middle of your lane. Moving closer to the passing rider is dangerous.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids, you should:

options.text: Keep the front brake on and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake on and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it again gently.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again gently.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should new riders position themselves?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: New riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them without having the new rider lead the group.
